response: {"title":"Diff-branch verification","intervention":"Verify every newly introduced conditional or exception path in the diff with the cheapest executable check that reaches it before spending time on unchanged-path regression tests, and abandon any check whose projected runtime would cross the deadline.","claim":"Compared with no appended instruction, prioritizing changed branches will increase hidden-test pass_rate without increasing deadline misses on multi-module Python tasks.","mechanism":"New branches have high defect priors and are often missed by happy-path tests; reaching each with the cheapest check maximizes novel behavioral evidence per unit time while the deadline gate bounds execution.","assumptions":["New conditional and exception paths are visible in the final diff.","The agent can choose a focused executable check for most new paths.","Projected test runtimes can be conservatively estimated."],"risks":["Cross-module regressions can arise without new branches.","Exhaustively identifying paths may consume excessive reasoning turns.","Runtime projection may be inaccurate.","Cheap synthetic checks may not reproduce production state or sequencing."],"test_plan":{"experiment":"Run a randomized matched-task A/B test with identical fixed deadlines, model, tools, and hidden-test scoring, appending the instruction only in treatment.","metrics":["pass_rate","wall_time","turns"],"success_condition":"Treatment yields higher pass_rate with no increase in deadline-miss rate; wall_time and turns are reported to assess verification overhead."},"single_shot_ordinal":5}
